title: Platform Sales Pilot Responsibility Matrix (draft)
content:
Purpose

This is a working sketch of a responsibility matrix and lightweight playbook for Platform Sales during customer pilots. The intent is practical: reduce handoff friction, make SLAs and fallbacks explicit, and give sellers / SEs a short checklist that maps to technical owners and operational actions.

Audience
- Platform Sellers (field SE, AE)
- Platform Onboarding / Solutions Engineering
- SRE / Running the Dedicated & Private stacks
- Product Ops (console, quotas, rollout)

Status notes (why this exists)
- We repeatedly see pilots stall in week 1 due to unclear routing for: model selection, latency anomalies, quota errors, and onboarding ETA for reserved capacity.
- This doc focuses on the first 30 days of a pilot and covers people + play actions (not an SLA contract).
- Draft -> iterate with SEs after two pilots.

Matrix (90s read)
- Seller / AE: customer contact, scope alignment, commercial terms (credits, limited reserved capacity), gather POC success criteria, sign-off on demo data access
- Field SE: integration checklist owner, sample prompt set creation, latency/cost targets with customer, primary demo and canary config, runbook author
- Solutions Eng (SE-SW): agent / workflow mapping, function/tool call expectations, golden prompts, model/filtering rules, failover model list
- Onboarding Engineer: account provisioning, keys/KMS handshake, network allowlists, VPC peering guidance, initial infra sizing recommendation
- Infra/SRE: capacity reservation in Dedicated (if requested), monitoring hooks, alert thresholds and escalation, KV/prefix cache priming, fallback policies enabled
- Product Ops / Console: enable debug tracing for the account, per-route telemetry, quota window adjustments, token/cost visibility for the AE
- Security/Compliance SME: DSR handling, PII mask config, audit log access, data retention agreement

Playbook: Day-by-day condensed
- Day 0 (pre-kick): Seller completes Pilot Intake form (link in linked artifacts) and tags product-op owner. Provide sample data and 3 golden prompts.
- Day 1: Kickoff call with AE, SE, onboarding engineer, customer infra contact. Agree success criteria and baseline perf (p95 latency, tokens/min, cost/run). SE to create an Integration Jira and move into onramp board.
- Day 3: First smoke test done by Field SE using customer sample prompts. If latency > target or errors appear, follow Rapid Triage below.
- Day 7: Canaries run from two regions. Solutions Eng to confirm fallback model is configured and KV cache policy is tested.
- Day 14: Review with customer — share cost telemetry and response-quality samples. Decide on next-stage (scale, reserved capacity, or stop).

Rapid Triage (who does what when something breaks)
- Symptom: Increased 5xx errors on Generation route
  - Field SE: capture example requests + IDs, set severity, notify Infra/SRE channel (tag @infra-oncall)
  - Infra/SRE: check model processes, GPU memory, kernel failures; look at recent config changes; escalate to Platform Ops if related to routing policies
  - Product Ops: look at rollout/canary config for model version mismatches

- Symptom: Latency spike (p95 > agreed target by 2x)
  - Field SE: reproduce via synthetic test, note sequence lengths and batch sizes
  - Infra/SRE: check batching queue depth, autoscaling events, GPU utilization; attempt failover to lower-latency compatible model if configured
  - Seller: communicate temporary mitigation and expected ETA to customer

Escalation ladder (short)
- T0: on-call infra (15m response) -> T1: infra lead & platform ops (30m) -> T2: Eng product manager + modeling team (2h)

Handoff checklist before scaling to Reserved Capacity
- Confirmed sample traffic pattern (QPS, seq len distribution)
- Verified prefix/KV caching behavior with real prompts
- Tracing enabled and sample traces collected for 10k tokens/day
- Security signoff for data movement and KMS configuration
- Pricing acknowledgement: expected tokens/day vs committed units (AE to confirm)

Slide mini-deck outline for the customer (5 slides)
1) Pilot Goals & Success Criteria (2 bullets max)
2) Quick Architecture Diagram (show model, caching, routing fallbacks)
3) What we measure (latency/cost/quality) + telemetry snapshot
4) Pilot timeline & escalation path (who to call)
5) Next steps and decision gate (scale vs optimize vs sunset)

Common seller snippets (short, usable)
- "We build in a canary fallback so if the primary model hits capacity your calls will automatically failover to a slightly smaller variant to keep user experience consistent."
- "We'll enable per-route token telemetry for 14 days so you can see exactly how unit costs are trending before we recommend reserving capacity."

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve
- Should every pilot have an infra cost cap enforced in the console, or do we leave it seller-configured? (ops/security tradeoff)
- What is the minimum sample size for quality checks (50 prompts? 200?)
- For private deployments, what's the standard window for KMS key rotation during pilots?

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Seller promises low latency without confirming sequence distribution -> Mitigation: mandatory synthetic run during Day 1 with customer's top 20 prompts
- Risk: Data residency or audit requirements slow down onboarding -> Mitigation: pre-approved compliance checklist & fast-path SOW template
- Risk: Pilot saturates shared hosted capacity -> Mitigation: temporary reserved slice or scheduled traffic windows

Short-term action items (owner + ETA)
- Create a one-click Pilot Intake template in Console (Product Ops) — owner: Rina Bhat — ETA: 2026-03-15
- Add a minimal SLA table to the seller playbook (Go-to-market) — owner: Maya Patel — ETA: 2026-03-05
- Draft a standard message for sellers to request 'capacity slice' from infra — owner: Diego Morales — ETA: 2026-03-03

Notes to self
- Keep this <2 pages when converted into a PDF cheat-sheet for sellers.
- We should A/B test two versions of the matrix: one for small pilots (<100k tokens/day) and one for enterprise (>1M tokens/day).

References and artifacts
- Pilot intake form (Confluence) — linked above
- Example Jira project: JIRA-1214 (onramp board)
- SE runbook skeleton: github.com/redwood/se-onboarding/runbook-template (PR teased in linked artifacts)

Next steps for collaborators
- Rina: confirm consent language for audit logs
- Diego: propose the infra slice workflow and command list
- Owen: validate the sample telemetry dashboard snapshot for Day 7

End of draft.

Revision history
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Maya)
- 2025-12-10: added rapid triage and escalation ladder (Diego)
- 2026-01-18: trimmed to 1-page cheat-sheet version (Rina)
